clue.text: It reflects note on recording, primarily

definitions.text: It reflects note on recording, primarily

indicators.note: in an across clue the turned note sits on, i.e. after, the recording's letter
primarily means only the first letter of the word recording is used
to reflect is to throw back, so the note's word is read backwards

parts.note: a breve is the longest note in music notation

explanation.surface: A music engineer explains a device that echoes each note on a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflects' means the musical note is read backwards, and 'on' puts it after the first letter of recording. Read whole, the clue also describes what the studio effect does.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverberation is sound bouncing back off surfaces, an echo effect added in studios.

clue.text: Leg breaks getting on top of a run scorer

indicators.note: in a down clue the reworked leg sits on top of what follows
breaks signals the letters of leg are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a leg-break bowler takes the wicket of a batsman who scores runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (leg breaks, run scorer) misleads: a scorer here is a composer who writes scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was an English composer, and a composer writes musical scores.

clue.text: Egg on toast at last for clubs and followers

indicators.note: one letter standing for another means the second replaces the first

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge or spur them
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: at last picks only the final letter of the word toast

explanation.surface: A breakfast instruction: put the egg on toast, with something about golf clubs and fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast at last for clubs' means the T that ends toast replaces C (clubs) in ENCOURAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants and hangers-on who trail a celebrity.

clue.text: Food's served up — with one lousy sprout

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: lousy means bad, signalling the letters of one are jumbled

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the food came with one louse-ridden sprout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns GRUB into BURG; 'lousy' rearranges ONE into EON.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to put out shoots or buds, a verb sense of sprouting.

clue.text: Amend bill? Barely

parts.note: an ad is an advertising bill or poster
just as in only just, by a small margin

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bill can be altered and is told it hardly can.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to alter it slightly, which is to amend it.

clue.text: Goddess, I gathered, turned up in Roman art

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the Latin word

parts.note: ars is the Latin word for art

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up reads the pair of words from the bottom

parts.note: met as in gathered together, assembled

explanation.surface: A visitor recognises a goddess while looking at Roman artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the phrase for 'I gathered', and 'in' puts the result inside the Latin word for art. The goddess is Greek despite the Roman setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis was the Greek deity of the hunt and the moon.

clue.text: Token gesture initially ignored by board supporting judge

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath the judge's letter
ignored means the letter is left out of the phrase for board

parts.note: to board a bus is to get on it

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word gesture

explanation.surface: A symbolic gesture from a panel is overlooked by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: GET ON (board) loses G, the initial of gesture, leaving ETON, which sits under J. 'Token gesture' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeton is a counter or metal disc used in place of a coin, a kind of token.

clue.text: Bridge player at restaurant needs a diamond maybe for trick

parts.note: S for South, one of the four seats at a bridge table
trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
a diamond is one example of a gem

explanation.surface: A bridge player at dinner wants a diamond to make a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are North, South, East and West, so S stands for a player. The diamond and trick sound like card play, but the diamond is a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or ruse, a trick to deceive.

clue.text: Location of Stamford Bridge? I give up

parts.note: to bridge two things is to connect them
taken as written
to cut out a habit is to give it up

explanation.surface: A frustrated quizzer can't place Stamford Bridge and gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamford Bridge is Chelsea's football ground in London, but here Stamford is the city in the US state and Bridge is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamford is a city on the coast of this New England state.

clue.text: Anything can be hard if unstarted with little time to finish

indicators.note: unstarted means the opening letter is taken from the front of the word for hard
to finish says where the letter taken from the front of the word goes: the very end

parts.note: tough means hard, difficult
T is the abbreviation for time, naming the letter that moves

explanation.surface: Advice that any task can seem hard if it is never begun and time runs short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstarted' takes the opening T off the word for hard, and 'with little time to finish' puts that T (time) at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is an old spelling of aught, meaning anything at all, as in 'for ought I know'.

clue.text: Turning American politician corrupt takes precedence

indicators.note: takes precedence means this piece goes in front of the others

parts.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A US politician who goes bad and pushes to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the American is a politician, but the A and TORY are separate pieces, with ROT placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory describes motion around an axis, like a wheel spinning.

clue.text: How to get techie to overcome awkwardness?

parts.note: rearranging the letters of the phrase the ice produces the word techie, so breaking it gets techie

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to win over a shy technical expert.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'break' is an anagram signal and THE ICE is its fodder, which gives TECHIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease initial tension in a social meeting is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Turn off by river to find food

indicators.note: off means wrong or spoilt, so the letters of turn are rearranged

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A traveller takes a turning by the river to get something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TURN to NURT; URE is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurture can mean nourishment, the sustenance that helps something grow.

clue.text: Part of a PC's watch

definitions.meaning: the screen of a personal computer

explanation.definitionFit: A computer's display screen has this name, and to observe something closely is the verb.

clue.text: Inmate leads head of gaol a dance

indicators.note: leads means the inmate's word goes at the front

parts.note: con is slang for convict, a prison inmate

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of gaol

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner leads the prison governor in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance where people follow a leader.

clue.text: Chap keeps working with standard type size

indicators.note: keeps means the name holds other letters inside it

parts.note: Neil is a man's name, a chap
on as in switched on, in operation
par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: A man stays at work with a fixed format for printing.
explanation.walkthrough: The working-plus-standard pair splits the name after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil is an old printers' name for a small font of six points.

clue.text: Recollection of a lost age, mostly pining at heart?

definitions.text: Recollection of a lost age, mostly pining at heart?

indicators.note: re-collection, gathering the letters again into a fresh order
mostly means the last letter of age is dropped
at heart takes the middle letters of the word pining

explanation.surface: A wistful memory of a vanished era, felt deep down as longing.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of pining is NI; 'Recollection' is both the anagram signal and part of the definition, and the A sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for the past.

clue.text: Fortress is a place to keep grain back after harvest

indicators.note: after means the turned word comes after the harvest

parts.note: taken as written
a crop is a harvest

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a silo is a tower for storing grain

explanation.surface: A fortress is described as somewhere grain is stored after harvesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SILO into OLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified citadel on the high ground of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: He should look after draughts player in team after winning regularly

indicators.note: after means the player comes behind the picked letters
regularly takes every other letter of the word winning

parts.note: a keeper, such as a goalkeeper, is a team player

explanation.surface: A board-game player who belongs to a winning team.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of wInNiNg give INN. Draughts are not the board game but drinks of draught beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican serves draught beer and so looks after the drinks.

clue.text: A fight in the toilets, the Ladies, among others?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, a fit of rage in the loo, read like road rage with pee
titled women such as Lady so-and-so belong to the nobility

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a jokey split, PEE plus RAGE, like road rage in a lavatory; 'the Ladies' looks like the toilets but means noblewomen.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers and peeresses, including those styled Lady, collectively form this rank.

clue.text: Ram front of Rolls into back of car and need a refitting?

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of Rolls
refitting signals the letters being put back together in a new arrangement
back of picks the last letter of car

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce shunts into the back of a car, which will need repair.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rolls's R leads, and the rest is a rearrangement of R, NEED and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear-end is to drive into the back of another vehicle, to ram it from behind.

clue.text: Brief wants to turn the clock back

indicators.note: back says the word for the clock being turned is read in reverse

parts.note: a timer is a clock you turn to set, like a kitchen timer; with back, the phrase also reads as reversing it

explanation.surface: Someone wishes they could reverse time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn the clock back' reads as winding time backwards, but here 'back' reverses the word for a turnable clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of responsibility given to someone, their brief.

clue.text: A French boxing ace, fighting, becomes unconscious

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing other letters

parts.note: une is the French for a (feminine)
A is the card abbreviation for ace
war means fighting

explanation.surface: A French boxing champion, mid-fight, gets knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: French une is the feminine form of a; 'boxing' puts the ace and the fighting inside it, and the boxing surface hints at a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unaware is not to know or notice, which is a sense of being unconscious of something.

clue.text: Greek's beset by past difficulties

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by the other letters

parts.note: ago means in the past
GR is an abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: Greece is surrounded by past difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for trouble or hassle.

clue.text: A drug smuggler conceals most of drug in this container

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: conceals means the smuggler's word hides other letters

parts.note: a mule is someone who carries drugs across borders

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A drug courier hides most of the drugs inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of the second drug, and 'conceals' tucks what remains inside the courier; the first 'drug' belongs to 'drug smuggler'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule is a small sealed glass vial holding a dose of medicine.

clue.text: Fellow's banned from entertaining with joke? Restore freedom of speech!

indicators.note: banned from means the letter is removed

parts.note: fun means entertaining
F is the abbreviation for fellow
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A comedian banned from performing protests for free speech.
explanation.walkthrough: FUN without F leaves UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ungag is to remove a gag, letting someone speak again.

clue.text: Beadle's About netting little gross capital

indicators.note: netting means catching the other letters inside
about signals that the letters of beadle are turned around into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
GR is the abbreviation for gross

explanation.surface: A TV prank show traps a modest gross in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Beadle's About was a British TV prank show hosted by Jeremy Beadle. 'About' rearranges BEADLE to BELADE, which nets GR.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia.

clue.text: Record industry's beginning to see sound reason

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of industry's
sound means say the word see and write what it sounds like

parts.note: the word see is pronounced like the letter C

explanation.surface: A music-business record starts to show good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Record industry looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoned argument, the principles of sound thinking.

clue.text: What mural covering conceals?

indicators.note: conceals means the letters are lying within the words mural covering

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what lies behind a painted wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run inside muRAL COVEring; a mural could indeed cover a recess.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in a wall, which a mural might cover.

clue.text: Cook with herb, the correct amount

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
sage is a herb

explanation.surface: A recipe says to cook with a herb, in the right quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the prescribed measure of medicine.
